phase_name: Defect-exposing cases, run RED against the unmodified hook

objectives.description: Observed false positive verbatim (multi-line essential-refactor subject) + single-line control
Hyphenated-prose cases single/multi-line for essential-refactor, auto-repair, multi-task, plus un-edged/repo-wide controls
One message-text false-positive case per vulnerable destructive detector, plus 2 multi-line variants
Comment-strip over-reach guard (unquoted # in real destructive command path)

approaches_tried.description: Message-text false-positive cases for detectors 3-7 phrased as ordinary prose with the destructive phrase mid-sentence (e.g. 'revert the git reset --hard fallout')
approaches_tried.reason: Detectors 3-7 read raw $COMMAND and anchor segment/match extraction on (^|[;&|][[:space:]]*) -- start-of-string or a literal ;/&/| character. Ordinary prose preceding the destructive phrase (e.g. 'the ') does not satisfy this anchor, so these cases were GREEN pre-fix -- not evidence of the defect, per the plan's own instruction to fix a defective case rather than keep it. Reproduced empirically outside the suite first (via a standalone script, to avoid tripping the deployed guard on the repo's own dirty tree -- see the SELF-REFERENTIAL HAZARD note below), then replaced in-suite with semicolon-punctuated phrasing that does reproduce RED.

notes: SELF-REFERENTIAL HAZARD fired for real: an early ad hoc reproduction run directly via the Bash tool (embedding literal '; git reset --hard' text in the raw multi-line command string) was blocked (exit 2) by the harness's own deployed guard-destructive-git.sh, because this repo's working tree was dirty (new untracked test file) at the time. Worked around by writing the reproduction to a script file and invoking it via `bash <file>`, keeping the trigger text out of the literal Bash tool command argument.
